So if you return an opened item, you'd receive up to 85% of the original price back rather than a full refund. If the item were unopened, no restocking fee would apply and you'd get the full amount back.
expected: Cascade Audio has opted into restocking fees, so per cw-restocking-fees and the store's policy page an opened item can be charged up to 15 percent. The agent must state the fee and cite both documents.
notes: The answer is correct and cited, but it exposes a gap the specification never resolves. facts.yaml publishes restocking_fee_max_percent: 15, the corpus publishes it per store, and stores.restocking_fee_opt_in records which stores opted in (5 Cascade Audio, 15 Second Stitch Apparel) - but nothing in agent/ or seed/eligibility.py reads that column, and SPEC.md's issue_refund contract never mentions restocking. So the agent promises 85% while issue_refund has no fee logic: the model either passes the full amount, contradicting what it just told the customer, or computes 85% itself, which puts a policy number in the model's hands with no record to audit. Marked met_requirement true because the agent answered the policy question correctly; problem_source is specification because the rule has no implementation anywhere.
